Adding data from a normal single-user Windows install (opencode desktop 1.18.30) that matches this pattern. Not a power-user/huge setup.

Database size breakdown (`opencode.db`):

- Total DB: ~2.36 GB
- `event` table alone: ~2.03 GB (149,137 rows)

Rows / bytes by event type:

| type | rows | size |
|---|---|---|
| `message.updated.1` | 37,664 | ~1,487 MB |
| `message.part.updated.1` | 99,943 | ~538 MB |
| `session.updated.1` | 11,318 | ~6 MB |
| `message.removed.1` | 119 | ~0.01 MB |
| `session.created.1` | 95 | ~0.04 MB |

Key observations:

- **Orphaned events = 0.** Every event's `aggregate_id` still exists in `session`, so a prune that only removes orphaned events (as proposed in #43456) would reclaim nothing here. The growth is *live-session historical snapshots*, not orphans.
- **A single session dominates**: one session accounts for ~1,309 MB across 2,126 events (~616 KB/event average) — a handful of very large snapshots drive most of the size.
- The `event` table has **no timestamp column**, so time-based retention is not possible without a schema change; only superseding-snapshot compaction (keep the newest snapshot per aggregate, drop superseded ones) helps.

This is consistent with the "full message snapshots stored on every streaming update with no retention" root cause, and confirms ~2 GB is reachable in ordinary use, not just the 13–51 GB reports.

Separately (context, not DB size): long sessions also get slow because the full history is resent each turn; `compaction.prune` defaults to `false`. Setting it to `true` mitigates the slowdown.

Confirming this on `opencode2 v0.0.0-beta-19425` with a different provider (Ollama through the OpenAI-compatible `/v1` shim). Three things to add that may help narrow it.

**1. The JSON route fails the same way, not just agent frontmatter.**

`opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "agents": { "implementer": { "model": "ollama/qwen3.6:35b-a3b" } },
  "model": "ollama/qwen3.8:latest"
}
```

`opencode2 debug agents` resolves it correctly:

```
implementer  subagent  ollama/qwen3.6:35b-a3b
```

The run uses the session model:

```
$ opencode2 run --standalone --agent implementer "Reply with exactly: PING."
> implementer · qwen3.8:latest
```

Frontmatter `model:` behaves identically. `--model` is honoured, as reported.

**2. The task tool dispatch path is affected too, which #36250 and #44680 also report.**

I verified this on the wire rather than from the banner, by putting a logging proxy in front of the provider and reading the `model` field of each request body. A parent agent dispatching a pinned subagent produced:

```
2 requests  model=qwen3.8:latest    (parent)
1 request   model=qwen3.8:latest    (subagent, should have been qwen3.6:35b-a3b)
```

Worth measuring this way. The `title` agent's pin **is** honoured, so the pinned model does get loaded at the end of most runs. Anyone checking `ollama ps` after a run will see the small model resident and conclude the pin worked. It did not.

**3. `agents.<name>.request.body.model` is not a workaround.**

The resolved agent carries a `request: { settings, headers, body }` block, so overriding the body model looks like a way out. It never reaches the provider: the proxy still logged the session model.

**Workaround that does work**, for anyone blocked on this. A plugin hook below the layer that drops the pin:

```ts
await ctx.session.hook("http.request", async (input) => {
  const wanted = pins.get(input.agent)      // input.agent is the agent id
  if (!wanted) return
  const original = input.request
  const body = JSON.parse(await original.text())
  if (body.model === wanted) return
  body.model = wanted
  input.request = new Request(original.url, {
    method: original.method,
    headers: original.headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  })
})
```

`SessionHttpRequest.request` is mutable and the input carries the agent id, so the correct model can be restored per agent. Confirmed working on both `run --agent` and a task tool dispatch. The banner still shows the session model.

**Impact for us:** every mechanical role in our pipeline silently ran on the large model. Nothing in the CLI, the config dump, or the banner disagreed with the config, so the only way to notice was the throughput meter showing a single model across an entire session.
I just checked this out and can verify it works as intended. Would be happy to see this merged.

Confirmed on **Windows / OpenCode Desktop 1.18.30** with the same failure mode after moving and renaming a Git project while preserving `.git`.

Before repair, the SQLite state was:

- `project.id`: unchanged and reused for the moved repository
- `project.worktree`: old deleted directory
- `project.sandboxes`: contained the new directory
- `project_directory.directory`: contained the new directory
- Three existing `session.directory` values: old deleted directory

Selecting the new project successfully initialized and watched the new path, but opening existing chats also created an instance for the deleted path and immediately logged `PlatformError: NotFound: FileSystem.realPath (...)`, caused by `ENOENT`. From the UI, chats appeared to end abruptly.

A local workaround was to back up `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`, update the matching `project.worktree`, `session.directory`, and matching non-empty `session.path` values to the new directory, then restart Desktop. `PRAGMA integrity_check` returned `ok`, all three sessions were preserved, and no active project/session route still referenced the deleted location.

This confirms the issue is not macOS-specific and that updating only `sandboxes` / `project_directory` is insufficient for existing sessions.

We have the inverse use case for the same configuration surface: coding-agent turns can have side effects, so we need `maxRetries: 0` to guarantee that the session processor does not implicitly replay a provider request.

On OpenCode 1.18.30, setting the provider/AI SDK retry count to zero does not disable `SessionRetry.policy()`. With injected retryable header/chunk transport failures we observed multiple primary provider requests. A global or per-provider `maxRetries` option that explicitly accepts zero would cover this case while preserving the current default for other users.

We are keeping our integration on unmodified upstream source in the meantime: the outer client reports failure and never automatically replays the Prompt, but it cannot promise a single provider attempt until this is configurable.
Closing this as a duplicate of #43596. I added the distinct `maxRetries: 0` / side-effecting coding-agent use case to that issue so the requirement is tracked in one place.

Iit is completely fixable!
In fact, the warning message itself tells us the exact solution:
MaxListenersExceededWarning: ... 11 drain listeners added to [WriteStream]. Use events.setMaxListeners() to increase limit

Why It Happens & How the Fix Works
1. The Cause: Node.js and Bun have a built-in default safety threshold of 10 listeners per stream. When OpenCode's multi-agent / parallel tasks queue 11  writes simultaneously, it exceeds that default by 1.
2. The Fix: Calling events.setMaxListeners(50) at startup raises this threshold from 10 to 50 across the entire OpenCode process.
• 11 listeners will be well below the limit of 50.
• The warning will never trigger or clutter your screen again.

Also reproduced in **OpenCode Web on Windows, using Microsoft Edge**, with server version **1.18.30** confirmed through `GET /global/health`. Adding the Web reproduction and read-side findings here rather than opening another duplicate.

### Reproduction

1. Open a non-Git directory (the project/current endpoint resolves it to `id: "global"`).
2. Open Edit Project, change the name, and click Save.
3. The dialog closes, but the project still displays the directory/fallback name.
4. Reopening Edit Project shows the old/fallback name again.

### Read-side findings

The v1.18.30 source and the actual JavaScript bundle served by the local server indicate a missing metadata merge, rather than necessarily a failed save:

- [`edit-project.ts`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.18.30/packages/app/src/components/edit-project.ts) takes the global/no-ID branch and calls `serverCtx().sync.project.meta(worktree, patch)` before closing the dialog.
- [`child-store.ts`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.18.30/packages/app/src/context/global-sync/child-store.ts), in `projectMeta()`, updates the persisted metadata cache and the child store's `projectMeta`.
- [`layout.tsx`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.18.30/packages/app/src/context/layout.tsx), in `enrich()`, builds the displayed project from server project metadata and the local project entry, but does not merge `childStore.projectMeta`. It separately handles `childStore.icon`.
- Inspection of the actually served `/assets/index-BpB7SL4b.js` found **two** enrichment paths with the omission: the server-context project list and the layout project list. Fixing only one path may leave another view stale.

This also matches the read-side analysis previously described in #42853. I have not independently verified the storage-key mismatch theory mentioned in other reports.

### Locally tested workaround

A browser DevTools Local Overrides patch was applied to both enrichment paths. Conceptually, after constructing the base project, it merges only the presentation/command metadata for global/unidentified projects:

```ts
if (
  (!projectID || projectID === "global") &&
  (!base.id || base.id === "global") &&
  childStore.projectMeta
) {
  const meta = childStore.projectMeta
  Object.assign(base, {
    name: meta.name ?? base.name,
    icon: { ...base.icon, ...meta.icon },
    commands: { ...base.commands, ...meta.commands },
  })
}
// Preserve the existing separate childStore.icon override afterwards.
```

The guard preserves Git-project metadata and does not replace project identity or directory fields. An empty custom name remains empty so that the existing directory-name fallback can work.

**Verification:** after enabling the local override in Edge, I tried renaming again and confirmed that the name is retained. The patch also passed 26 isolated function-level assertions covering both paths (name, empty name, color, commands, icon precedence, Git-project preservation, repeated reads), plus a syntax check of the full patched JavaScript. These automated checks are **not** a full browser E2E suite, and the workaround is **not** an upstream source build.

Suggested upstream direction: consistently consume the persisted local `projectMeta` in both project-enrichment paths for global/non-Git projects, with regression coverage for saving, reopening the edit dialog, and reloading the Web UI.

Related: #36944 documents the over-report side of the same fork cost-accounting mechanism — forked sessions double-count inherited history while the parent session is alive.

This issue is the under-report counterpart: the same anti-double-counting logic means a fork does not count its parent's history, so when the parent session is deleted, those inherited messages are the only record of that spend and it silently disappears from stats. Verified against the provider console: stats reported $1.90 for a day the provider billed ~$5 (the $2.90 gap was exactly a fork's inherited history).

Note for the fix of #36944: a naive dedup of pre-fork messages would introduce this under-report case. The rule that matched provider billing in our data excludes inherited history only while the parent session still exists.

Heads-up: this PR's fork-zeroing fixes the over-count (#36944) but doesn't cover the deleted-parent case (#48306). After zeroing, an orphan fork's inherited spend becomes unrecoverable even from message-level data. Consider preserving deleted-session aggregates (rollup) or reattributing inherited cost at fork time.

### Summary
    When streaming responses or running concurrent prompt tasks under high load or concurrency, OpenCode's bundled Bun runtime triggers a
  `MaxListenersExceededWarning` on `node:fs` `WriteStream` for the `"drain"` event.

    On Windows (especially PowerShell), this warning emitted to `stderr` causes PowerShell to treat it as a `NativeCommandError`, interrupting
  or polluting the TUI / terminal interface.

    ---

    ### Environment
    - **OS:** Windows 10/11 x64
    - **OpenCode Version:** `1.18.30` (Bun standalone binary build)
    - **Runtime:** Bun (bundled internal runtime)

 ### Root Cause Analysis

  1. In getPrompt / send / request, Effect's concurrent stream evaluation attaches a one-time "drain" event listener via once("drain", ...) to
  the underlying WriteStream whenever the stream buffer fills.
  2. Because multiple tasks/chunks evaluate concurrently in parallel fibers, the number of simultaneous pending "drain" listeners regularly
  exceeds the default EventEmitter threshold (default is 10).
  3. Even when raised to 50 in custom plugins, burst concurrency hit 51 listeners and re-triggered the warning.
  4. Because the drain listener is attached with once(...), listeners are cleaned up as soon as backpressure drains—this is not an actual
  memory leak, but normal high concurrency hitting the default sanity check.
  ──────
  ### Suggested Fixes in OpenCode Core

  Any of the following solutions in OpenCode will resolve this:

  1. Option A (Preferred - Target the Stream):
  In the stream writer / sink module before attaching write listeners:
    // In the module creating or wrapping the WriteStream
    stream.setMaxListeners(0); // or a high ceiling like 100+

  2. Option B (Process Level):
  In the OpenCode bootstrap entrypoint:
    import events from "node:events";
    events.defaultMaxListeners = 100; // or events.setMaxListeners(0)

  3. Option C (Bun / CLI launcher):
  Ensure CLI entry wrappers pass --no-warnings or handle warning events so benign EventEmitter overflow warnings do not leak to stderr and
  crash/pollute PowerShell host sessions.

## Reproduced with Gmail on macOS

### Environment

- OpenCode CLI: 1.18.25, installed globally from the `opencode-ai` npm package
- OpenCode beta runtime: 0.0.0-beta-19192
- OS: Darwin 25.5.0, arm64
- Terminal: `xterm-256color`
- Shell: `/bin/zsh`
- Active plugins: none found
- MCP server: `https://gmailmcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1`

### Reproduction

1. Configure the Gmail remote MCP server. In this case the server has no explicit OAuth client ID or secret, so OpenCode attempts dynamic client registration.
2. Run `opencode mcp auth gmail`.
3. OpenCode prints `Authentication successful!`, although no Google consent page is completed and the Gmail entry in `~/.local/share/opencode/mcp-auth.json` is empty.
4. Run `opencode mcp auth list`; Gmail remains `not authenticated`.
5. Call any Gmail tool, including `list_labels` or `get_thread`.

### Actual behaviour

Every Gmail tool call fails consistently with:

```text
Incompatible auth server: does not support dynamic client registration
```

The MCP extensions screen shows only an enable/disable toggle, so it offers no route to enter the pre-registered OAuth client credentials that Google's hosted MCP servers require.

Google Calendar and Google Drive show the same unauthenticated state. Other remote MCP servers, including Notion, authenticate and execute correctly.

### Expected behaviour

OpenCode should not report authentication success when no token was obtained or persisted. For an authorization server that does not support dynamic client registration, it should give an actionable error before claiming success, such as requiring `oauth.client_id` and `oauth.client_secret` and pointing the user to configuration.

Google documents that its hosted Workspace MCP servers do not support dynamic client registration, so the current success message leaves the user unable to distinguish a missing static OAuth client configuration from a completed login.

Hit the server-side twin of this and found the root cause — sharing in case
it helps the fix.

**Setup:** ~35 project dirs under one parent, each created by duplicating an
existing dir (`cp -r`), served via `opencode web` on 1.18.30.

**Symptom:** opening project B's web URL showed project A in the header, and
new sessions created there were *actually assigned* to project A's ID — not
just mislabeled. Worse: deleting the bad `project_directory` rows and
reassigning sessions in `opencode.db` reverted within seconds; the server
re-wrote the wrong rows on its own.

**Root cause (traced in the 1.18.30 binary):** project resolution precedence is
`git-remote-derived ID > .git/opencode file content > root-commit SHA`.
`cp -r` had copied project A's `.git/opencode` (containing A's project ID)
into B, and that file **outranks the entire database**. `fromDirectory` then
upserts the wrong row and `migrateProjectId(previous → current)` retags B's
sessions *and* mappings to A — the self-healing I was seeing. So beyond the
`projectForSession` display lookup, anything that duplicates a project dir
poisons identity at the source.

**Fix that held:**
1. In each project dir, verify `.git/opencode` holds that project's *own* ID
   (cross-check against the `project` table / `GET /project`).
2. Write the correct project ID into every mismatched file (36 projects, zero
   clashes after the fix).
3. **Prevention:** after any `cp -r` of a project dir, `rm -f .git/opencode`
   before first launch.
4. Restart the server afterwards — mappings are cached in memory.

**Suggested hardening:** `migrateProjectId` could refuse (or at least warn)
when the source of the ID collision is a `.git/opencode` file whose directory
doesn't match the project's recorded worktree - right now a stale anchor file
silently rewrites the DB to match itself.

`openai/codex`'s own bundled catalog, [`codex-rs/models-manager/models.json`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/968835997714baaff199cfed5f89a2c65d8ca77d/codex-rs/models-manager/models.json), now reports two separate fields per model, not one:

```json

{"slug": "gpt-6-astra", "context_window": 272000, "max_context_window": 872000, "supports_experimental_context": true}
```

`context_window` is the number [#36248](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/36248) and [#39082](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/39082) copied into the [hardcoded override in codex.ts](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/b3f1a96c6dd7adeb28b36dd11add1998fc84d67b/packages/opencode/src/plugin/openai/codex.ts#L315-L322). `max_context_window` isn't read anywhere in opencode, and at 872,000 it's much closer to the 921,858-token ceiling this issue's binary search actually measured. It's tied to a real, shipped OpenAI feature too: [Experimental context management](https://developers.openai.com/codex/models), opt-in via `features.context_management.experimental_mode = true` in `config.toml`, available to ChatGPT Plus/Pro sign-in. So the catalog already distinguishes a default UI budget from a ceiling the client can request, and opencode is only reading the former as if it were the hard endpoint limit, which matches this issue's own conclusion.

Anyone paying for Plus/Pro specifically to avoid separate API billing is taking a silent, substantial usability hit versus using Codex CLI directly or switching to an API key, and it's easy to mistake for opencode being broken rather than for a stale clamp.

Reproduced on opencode **1.18.30** (macOS 26.6.2 arm64) with **cua-driver 0.26.0** (Rust/schemars MCP server, 34 tools with `outputSchema`). `opencode mcp list` prints 81 warning lines covering 26 unique schema paths, so it reproduces outside the TUI too.

Root cause is in the SDK's output-schema validation path, not the AI SDK `jsonSchema()` conversion:

- `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.29.0` `Client.listTools()` eagerly compiles every tool `outputSchema` through `AjvJsonSchemaValidator` (`cacheToolMetadata`). Input schemas are never Ajv-compiled, which is why #12815/#20747 (stripping formats before `jsonSchema()`) can't suppress these warnings.
- Ajv ignores unknown formats but its default logger calls `console.warn` during compilation, so `--log-level` doesn't help and the raw lines hit the terminal.

Verified fix: supply a `jsonSchemaValidator` through the SDK's documented `ClientOptions` seam, using an Ajv with the SDK's defaults plus `logger: false`:

```ts
const ajv = new Ajv({ strict: false, validateFormats: true, validateSchema: false, allErrors: true, logger: false })
addFormats(ajv)
const CLIENT_OPTIONS = {
  // capabilities...
  jsonSchemaValidator: new AjvJsonSchemaValidator(ajv),
} satisfies ClientOptions
```

With that, warning output goes to 0, while known formats (uuid, date-time, ...) and type validation are unchanged. I can open a PR with a unit test if this approach is acceptable.
